🐛 Describe the bug
Some tests in transformers compare 2 outputs and assert them are close. Although we know we can't guarantee the outputs are identical across torch versions, this time the situation is a bit worrying.
Previously, for some tests, the 2 outputs they compare have a difference in the magnitude of 1e-9, but now it is in the  magnitude of 1e-5. Below I provide 2 examples.
Of course, the difference in the magnitude of 1e-5 is acceptable, but the change from 1e-9 to 1e-5 seems strange, and potentially this affect many tests that compared to some expected outputs (integration tests).
The same error occurs 29 times in the CI suite for models running on single gpu. It seems that this happens for models with vision component (vit / clip / blip) etc.
(Totally, we get There are 527 new failed tests with torch 2.8 RC. Although I have to check other failed tests, I am thinking if mostly of them can be caused by this numerical issues? I will update the issue if I have any clue for other failed tests.)
It would be really nice if torch team can check if there is anything wrong here.
(before we spend the time to update the many tests' expected outputs in transformers 🙏 )

Hi team,
I'm working on a high-performance Apple Silicon M4 environment and have encountered a limitation when trying to install PyTorch 2.7.1 with MPS support.
While the version is available on PyPI, it is not yet published on the MPS-specific index:
https://download.pytorch.org/whl/mps
This prevents users from leveraging GPU acceleration via MPS on newer Apple hardware, despite the fact that the issue appears to be resolved in 2.7.1 (as confirmed by others on Hugging Face and GitHub forums).
Could you please clarify:

Whether a build for 2.7.1 with MPS support is planned?
If so, is there an estimated timeline for its release?

This would be extremely helpful for developers working on Apple Silicon M3/M4 systems who rely on MPS for production-level inference and training.
Thanks in advance,
Juan Alberto Ignacio Videla
Buenos Aires - Argentina

nodes.title: Why is there such a big difference in size between the torch CUDA 12.6 whl and the cuda 12.9 whl? Why is only the 12.6 whl package placed on the PyPI source?
The opp is not compatible with compile mode="reduce-overhead" and linear layers for large inputs.

PyTorch internally might have  trigger a one-time warning in test_linspace_logspace. That could be the same warning the other test (test_tensor_with_grad_to_scalar_warning) is trying to catch, but it's already been triggered and silenced in test_linspace_logspace.

    def __init__(self):

        self.text_emb = nn.Embedding(100, 100).to("cuda")
        # self.speech_emb = nn.Embedding(100, 100).to("cuda")
        # use _weight
        self.speech_emb = nn.Embedding(
            100, 100, _weight=self.text_emb.weight.clone(), _freeze=True
        ).to("cuda")
        self.bias = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(100)).to("cuda")
        # self.bias = torch.randn(100).to("cuda")
        # copy text_emb into a tensor
        self.text_emb_cache = self.text_emb.weight.clone()
        # self.speech_emb.weight.requires_grad = False
        # y = self.speech_emb.weight.clone()
        # self.speech_emb.weight = None
        # self.speech_emb.weight = y
        # self.speech_emb_cache = self.speech_emb.weight
        # self.speech_emb_cache = self.speech_emb.weight.clone()
        # self.speech_emb_cache = self.text_emb_cache.clone()
        # torch._dynamo.mark_static_address(self.text_emb.weight)
        # torch._dynamo.mark_static_address(self.speech_emb.weight)
        torch._dynamo.mark_static_address(self.text_emb_cache)
        # torch._dynamo.mark_static_address(self.speech_emb_cache)
        torch._dynamo.mark_static_address(self.speech_emb.weight)
        torch._dynamo.mark_static_address(self.bias)
        for i in range(5):
            setattr(self, f"layer_{i}", nn.Linear(100, 100).to("cuda"))
            torch._dynamo.mark_static_address(getattr(self, f"layer_{i}").weight)

    def forward(self, text, speech):
        text_emb = self.text_emb_cache[text]
        # speech_emb = self.speech_emb(speech)
        # speech_emb = self.speech_emb_cache[speech]
        speech_emb = self.speech_emb.weight[speech]
        text_emb = text_emb + self.bias
        for i in range(5):
            text_emb = getattr(self, f"layer_{i}")(text_emb)
            speech_emb = getattr(self, f"layer_{i}")(speech_emb)
        return text_emb, speech_emb


with torch.no_grad(), torch.inference_mode():

🐛 Describe the bug
Torch-TensorRT uses torch.export to get exported program, which then be decomposed using ep.run_decompositions. However, the decomposition fails in some cases with error message.
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/torch/export/_trace.py", line 897, in _maybe_fixup_gm_and_output_node_meta
    assert len(new_output_node.meta) == 0

We found that the node meta is stack_trace,
{'stack_trace': 'File "/workspace/TensorRT/py/torch_tensorrt/dynamo/runtime/_MutableTorchTensorRTModule.py", line 491, in forward\n    self.compile()'}

and it exists when a forward function is called in the trace of exporting the program. Can you fix this bug so we can export the program in a wrapper that has a forward function? This error shows up after June 26 so it must be recent updates that break this.
Reproduce Steps:
import os
import torch

import torchvision.models as models
from torch._decomp import get_decompositions as get_torch_decompositions

pyt_model = models.resnet18(pretrained=True).eval().to("cuda")
example_inputs = (torch.randn((128, 3, 224, 224)).to("cuda"),)


class Wrapper():
    def __init__(self, model, example_inputs):
        self.model = model
        self.example_inputs = example_inputs

    def compile(self):
        self.exp_program = torch.export.export(self.model, args=self.example_inputs)
        self.exp_program = self.exp_program.run_decompositions(get_torch_decompositions([torch.ops.aten.new_full]))
        print("OK")
        
    def forward(self, *args, **kwargs):
        self.compile()

wrapper = Wrapper(pyt_model, example_inputs)

wrapper.compile() ## OK
wrapper.forward() ## Error


The wrapper here is a simplified version of what we need in Torch-TensorRT.
Versions
PyTorch nightly: 2.8.0.dev20250626+cu128

🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch
Hi, I noticed that BatchNorm and InstanceNorm don't provide a bias: bool argument. I understand that affine=True with bias is standard design because these norms wipe out any feature/channel-wise bias added by the previous layer. However, this design makes it impossible to implement a Norm layer with only rescaling but no bias.
A similar issue exists with RMSNorm, which doesn't implement the bias term at all, let alone give the user a choice, even though the original paper explicitly defines the complete module as a

linear transformation (Linear/Conv) without bias (Eq. 1), then
normalization + affine map including bias (Eq. 2).

In contrast, LayerNorm supports both elementwise_affine: bool and bias: bool arguments. Similar to LayerNorm, GroupNorm doesn't completely wipe out the feature/channel-wise bias added in the previous layer either, yet the API doesn't give the option to turn its bias off.
I'd be happy to create a PR if someone can confirm that this would be a good feature to have.
